These vulnerabilities allow attackers to inject arbitrary HTML, attributes, and classes into content, leading to account hijacking, web content injection, page defacement, and redirection attacks. detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for mass publication of npm packages with minimal content and external links, especially those pointing to known malicious or scam domains. matched_snippet.code_behavior: At runtime, on page load or script execution, the code injects external scripts into the page, including a deprecated version of Ionicons and a remote script (slim.js) hosted on jsDelivr, which itself contains the trojanized jQuery. This enables further malicious code execution and persistence by loading additional payloads from attacker-controlled sources.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script injects remote code from attacker-controlled sources without user consent, using a misleading deprecation warning to disguise its activity and facilitate further compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not inject remote scripts or downgrade libraries without explicit user action or clear documentation. Core libraries should not dynamically load external code from untrusted sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic script injection is used in some legitimate plugin loaders, but not in core libraries or without user awareness and explicit opt-in.
key_indicators: Injection of remote scripts from suspicious or attacker-controlled domains
Phony deprecation warnings in console output to mislead users
Use of outdated or deprecated library versions
Chaining to further malicious payloads via dynamic script loading

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, on page load or script execution

package_info.package_versions: 8.0.0 (and dozens of others, see report for full list)
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a trojanized version of jQuery in which the 'end' prototype function is maliciously modified to exfiltrate all form data from the page to attacker-controlled domains whenever it is called, either directly or indirectly (e.g., via fadeTo). The package is distributed under many names and versions, often with additional suspicious files and unique exfiltration URLs, indicating a persistent, manually assembled supply chain attack targeting web applications.

attack_chain.action: User installs a malicious npm package containing a trojanized jQuery file (or similar).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is present in the project and loaded in the browser.

attack_chain.action: Trojanized jQuery is loaded and used in the web application.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious prototype function (end) is available in the global jQuery object.

attack_chain.action: User or application code calls fadeTo or end (directly or indirectly), triggering the malicious end function.
attack_chain.leads_to: Form data is serialized and exfiltrated to attacker-controlled domains.

attack_chain.action: Injected scripts (from icons.js/min.js) load additional remote payloads (e.g., slim.js) from jsDelivr, which may contain further trojanized code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Persistence and further compromise of the web application.

behavioral_signatures: Modification of jQuery prototype functions (especially end) to perform network requests
Exfiltration of serialized form data via AJAX to external domains
Dynamic injection of remote scripts from non-standard or outdated sources
Presence of phony deprecation warnings in console output
file_indicators: jquery.min.js, registration.min.js, icon.min.js, fontawesome.js, slim.js, all-min.js (with non-standard or unexpected content)
Presence of termux.properties, npm cache, or npm logs in package tarballs
network_indicators: Requests to domains such as *.truex.biz.id, *.hanznesia.my.id, *.api-system.engineer, *.jsdelivr.net/gh/indexsc/libs/slim.js, and other listed campaign domains
AJAX GET requests with hex-encoded form data in query parameters
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan JavaScript dependencies for modifications to core library prototype functions (e.g., jQuery.fn.end). Flag any code that serializes and exfiltrates form data to external domains. Monitor for dynamic script injection from non-standard or outdated sources, and alert on requests to known campaign domains. Review package contents for unexpected files (e.g., termux.properties, npm logs) and non-standard file naming patterns. Correlate behavioral, file, and network indicators to identify supply chain attacks.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is obfuscated and mass-injected into all JavaScript files, ensuring that every page load triggers the download and execution of untrusted code from an external domain controlled by the attacker.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate code should not inject remote scripts from unrelated or untrusted domains into all JavaScript files, especially using obfuscation and without user or developer consent.

key_indicators: Obfuscated JavaScript injected into all *.js files

No legitimate business logic—sole purpose is to load further code from an attacker-controlled domain
Script tag uses a unique id (hook-loader) to avoid duplicate injection

package_info.package_manager: GitHub (malicious commit, not a package manager)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (affects repositories via commit, not a package release)
package_info.why_malicious: The attack involves unauthorized commits impersonating Dependabot, introducing a malicious GitHub Actions workflow and modifying all JavaScript files to exfiltrate repository secrets and end-user credentials. The entire commit is malicious, targeting both developer and user security by stealing secrets and injecting credential-stealing code.

attack_chain.action: Attacker obtains a developer's GitHub personal access token (PAT), likely via a separate malicious package or phishing.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to authenticate as the victim and push code to their repositories.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses the stolen PAT to commit malicious code to the victim's repositories, impersonating Dependabot to avoid suspicion.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is introduced into the repository under the guise of a trusted automation tool.

attack_chain.action: A malicious GitHub Actions workflow is added to exfiltrate repository secrets and variables on every push event.
attack_chain.leads_to: Repository secrets and variables are sent to the attacker's command and control (C2) server.

attack_chain.action: All JavaScript files in the repository are modified to append an obfuscated script loader that fetches additional malicious code from an external domain.
attack_chain.leads_to: End-users of the web application are exposed to further malicious payloads when they load the compromised JavaScript files.

attack_chain.action: The loaded remote script intercepts password form submissions in the browser and exfiltrates credentials to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: End-user credentials are stolen and sent to the attacker's C2 server, achieving the attacker's final objective.

Mass modification of JavaScript (*.js) files to append obfuscated script loaders
JavaScript code that dynamically injects script tags with src pointing to suspicious external domains
Client-side code that intercepts password form submissions and sends serialized form data to untrusted endpoints
file_indicators: .github/workflows/hook.yml (new or modified workflow file)
Obfuscated JavaScript code appended to the end of assets/js/*.js files

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for new or modified GitHub Actions workflows that serialize and POST secrets or variables to external domains. Scan for mass changes to JavaScript files, especially for obfuscated code that injects remote scripts from send.wagateway.pro. Detect client-side code that attaches event listeners to password forms and exfiltrates credentials. Flag any network traffic to send.wagateway.pro domains as a high-confidence indicator of compromise.
